A cmux pane that IS a Barkpark worker: it claims the task it owns on session-start, renews the lease while the agent works, closes on proven acceptance, and lease-expires into a ↩ resume if it stops without proving doneness. One command — bp cmux dispatch — reads the wave-13 dispatch frontier and spawns a fresh agent pane per non-interfering pick. A client-side bp cmux builtin, no server or API change. The falsifiable claim: the bridge never false-closes unfinished work and never breaks the agent.

1. The wish

Open (or dispatch) a pane and it owns a task: claim on start, renew while working, close on proven acceptance, resume on drop. And dispatch the frontier into fresh panes with one keystroke. The whole bridge is intercepted in internal/cli/cli.go before manifest dispatch — exactly like bp tasks and bp task frontier. Go, testable, fail-safe. This phase is design-only and read-only — nothing on guerrilla is mutated.

2. What cmux gives us

cmux injects a protected, pane-life-invariant env: CMUX_SURFACE_ID (durable, pane-unique) plus CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID / CMUX_PANEL_ID / CMUX_TAB_ID. Its `claude` shim fires cmux claude-hook <event> per hook event; we run ALONGSIDE it via a second command bp cmux hook <event> added by install — we ADD, never replace.

Why surface-keyed, not session-keyed: the PANE owns the task, not the individual agent. CMUX_SURFACE_ID is invariant for the pane's life; CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID differs per agent and subagents share the pane's CMUX_* env. Keying the worker id on the surface means every subagent in the pane renews the SAME claim (re-claim under the same worker = renewal, not a 409), and the pane holds exactly one fencing lease.

3. The worker-id derivation

One function — taskboard.CmuxWorkerID() beside ResolveWorker in internal/taskboard/actions.go — honored everywhere. Four-tier precedence:

CmuxWorkerID(): 1. BARKPARK_WORKER_ID if set # explicit override; also what install sets 2. cmux-<CMUX_SURFACE_ID> if CMUX_SURFACE_ID set # durable pane-unique — the normal path 3. cmux-<CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID> if CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID set # coarser cmux fallback (pane-not-unique) 4. ResolveWorker() # existing tui-<hostname> convention (final fallback)

Tier 1 first means a hand-set worker id always wins; because ResolveWorker ALSO checks BARKPARK_WORKER_ID first, tier 1 and tier 4 are consistent. Tier 2 is load-bearing: pane-stable and cmux-scoped with no install step, so even an ad-hoc bp cmux status in a raw cmux pane reads correctly. The install shell-line export BARKPARK_WORKER_ID=cmux-$CMUX_SURFACE_ID feeds tier 1 so an in-pane bp invocation and the helper always agree.

4. The hook contract

bp cmux hook <event> reads the Claude hook JSON on stdin and the env (BARKPARK_TASK = the task this pane owns; worker = CmuxWorkerID). Event → action:

Claude eventOur actionDetail
SessionStartclaim BARKPARK_TASKDoClaim(client, task, worker). Re-claim under the same worker renews the lease (new epoch). Idempotent across subagents.
PreToolUserenew (re-claim), throttledAt most once per 60s via an on-disk stamp, well inside the 300s TTL. In-window → no request.
Stopclose IFF acceptance proven, else leaveRead the task; if it has ≥1 acceptance criterion and ALL are met → re-claim for the live epoch, then DoClose. Otherwise do NOTHING → lease expires → resume.
SessionEndsame as StopShares the close-attempt logic; a double close is harmless (the second gets not_ready/stale, exits 0).
Notification / UserPromptSubmitno-op, exit 0We don't act; cmux's hook may.
unknown / missingno-op, exit 0Never guess.
The honest close default — acceptance-gated, never turn-boundary. Stop fires at the END OF EVERY TURN, not "the task is done". Closing unconditionally on Stop would false-close an interactive multi-turn agent after its first turn. The rule that works for BOTH a one-shot dispatched agent AND an interactive pane: close only on PROVEN acceptance (≥1 acceptance_criteria entry and every one met==true). Anything else → do not close, do not renew → let the 300s lease expire → the built ↩ resume recovers it. A false resume is cheap; a false close strands unfinished work.

Re-claim-at-close (no persisted epoch): SessionStart and Stop are separate processes. Rather than persist the epoch, Stop re-claims (a renewal under our own worker id) to obtain the LIVE epoch, then closes with it — the same "press c to renew, then x" resync pattern actions.go already documents. Strictly more robust: if another worker grabbed the expired lease, our re-claim gets a 409 → we exit 0 and DON'T close (no theft). The only cross-process state is the PreToolUse throttle stamp under {config}/barkpark/cmux/, never the epoch. WHO sets met=true: the working agent, via bp task mutation during the session — the hook only READS the recorded state, it never judges.

The cardinal fail-safe rules

1. Every path exits 0 — success, error, unknown event, missing env, unreachable server, malformed stdin, panic (top-level recover → exit 0). A non-zero exit from a hook can abort or stall the agent's turn.
2. Nothing on stdout on the hook path — some Claude events feed hook stdout back into the agent's context. Diagnostics go to stderr only, under --dry-run or BP_CMUX_DEBUG.
3. Bounded network — a short ~4s timeout so a hung server never stalls a turn; timeout → no-op, exit 0. The 300s lease TTL is the backstop.
4. Missing BARKPARK_TASK → exit 0 — a pane that owns no task does nothing.
5. Can't read → can't prove — Get returns (Doc,false) on any read failure, so the acceptance gate treats unreadable as unproven → leave claimed (resume). Correct fail-safe direction.

5. Dispatch

bp cmux dispatch fetches the snapshot (FetchSnapshotFull), builds the board, and calls the SHARED taskboard.Frontier (IMPORTED, never reimplemented — dispatch never forks the interference model). Per pick it emits:

cmux new-surface --type agent-session \ --env BARKPARK_TASK=<pick.DocID> \ --prompt <taskPrompt(pick)>

Worker id is NOT passed at dispatch — the new surface's CMUX_SURFACE_ID does not exist until cmux creates the pane. We export BARKPARK_TASK only; the new pane's install shell-line derives its OWN BARKPARK_WORKER_ID from its freshly-injected surface id, and its SessionStart hook claims. A dispatched pane and a hand-attached pane derive their worker the identical way. Dry-run-first is the safety spine: --dry-run PRINTS the launch plan and spawns nothing; dry-run is the DEFAULT when cmux is absent from PATH; only when cmux is on PATH and --dry-run is off do we exec.Command(...).Start() (Start, never Wait). --max is the ambition dial (FrontierOpts.Max); --proven-only is the careful dial (spawn only the area-proven isolated set). Both mirror bp task frontier.

6. Install

Print-first, never clobber. --print is the DEFAULT: show the Claude Code settings.json hooks block (SessionStart/Stop/SessionEnd → bp cmux hook <event>; PreToolUse catch-all matcher → renew) plus the guarded shell line, with copy-paste instructions naming both ~/.claude/settings.json and the shell profile / cmux pane-init. Everything runs ALONGSIDE cmux's own hooks — the hooks map is additive per event.

A reserved --merge mode (designed, not slice-1) carefully folds our four hook entries into an existing ~/.claude/settings.json — deduped by exact command string, backed up first, diff printed, --yes required, idempotent, refuses on malformed JSON and falls back to --print. Kept out of slice 1 to honor the read-only posture.

7. Honest limits

• Dispatch quality is bounded by the frontier's area: coverage (3% today, wave-13's §5 hygiene arm), not by this bridge.
• The SessionStart-claim race (two dispatchers, or a human already on the task): today the loser's SessionStart claim just 409s and exits 0. The reserved claim-before-spawn dispatch (wave-13's atomic multi-claim) closes it.
• No heartbeat endpoint exists — liveness is renew-or-expire; the 300s TTL + task.lease_expired → resume is the whole model.
• The exact cmux new-surface flag spelling (--env vs -e, --prompt vs --initial-prompt, --type agent-session) is from feasibility research; dispatch is dry-run-first precisely so the operator eyeballs the invocation, and the slice confirms flags against cmux new-surface --help in one place.

Linked into the dispatch-frontier family — it consumes taskboard.Frontier (df-frontier-fn).

The cardinal fail-safe rules

  1. Every path exits 0 — success, error, unknown event, missing env, unreachable server, malformed stdin, panic (top-level recover → exit 0). A non-zero exit from a hook can abort or stall the agent's turn.
  2. Nothing on stdout on the hook path — some Claude events feed hook stdout back into the agent's context. Diagnostics go to stderr only, under --dry-run or BP_CMUX_DEBUG.
  3. Bounded network — a short ~4s timeout so a hung server never stalls a turn; timeout → no-op, exit 0. The 300s lease TTL is the backstop.
  4. Missing BARKPARK_TASK → exit 0 — a pane that owns no task does nothing.
  5. Can't read → can't prove — Get returns (Doc,false) on any read failure, so the acceptance gate treats unreadable as unproven → leave claimed (resume). Correct fail-safe direction.

5. Dispatch

bp cmux dispatch fetches the snapshot (FetchSnapshotFull), builds the board, and calls the SHARED taskboard.Frontier (IMPORTED, never reimplemented — dispatch never forks the interference model). Per pick it emits:

cmux new-surface --type agent-session \
  --env BARKPARK_TASK=<pick.DocID> \
  --prompt <taskPrompt(pick)>

Worker id is NOT passed at dispatch — the new surface's CMUX_SURFACE_ID does not exist until cmux creates the pane. We export BARKPARK_TASK only; the new pane's install shell-line derives its OWN BARKPARK_WORKER_ID from its freshly-injected surface id, and its SessionStart hook claims. A dispatched pane and a hand-attached pane derive their worker the identical way. Dry-run-first is the safety spine: --dry-run PRINTS the launch plan and spawns nothing; dry-run is the DEFAULT when cmux is absent from PATH; only when cmux is on PATH and --dry-run is off do we exec.Command(...).Start() (Start, never Wait). --max is the ambition dial (FrontierOpts.Max); --proven-only is the careful dial (spawn only the area-proven isolated set). Both mirror bp task frontier.

6. Install

Print-first, never clobber. --print is the DEFAULT: show the Claude Code settings.json hooks block (SessionStart/Stop/SessionEnd → bp cmux hook <event>; PreToolUse catch-all matcher → renew) plus the guarded shell line, with copy-paste instructions naming both ~/.claude/settings.json and the shell profile / cmux pane-init. Everything runs ALONGSIDE cmux's own hooks — the hooks map is additive per event.

# Barkpark: one worker id per cmux pane, derived from the durable surface id.
[ -n "$CMUX_SURFACE_ID" ] && export BARKPARK_WORKER_ID="cmux-$CMUX_SURFACE_ID"

A reserved --merge mode (designed, not slice-1) carefully folds our four hook entries into an existing ~/.claude/settings.json — deduped by exact command string, backed up first, diff printed, --yes required, idempotent, refuses on malformed JSON and falls back to --print. Kept out of slice 1 to honor the read-only posture.

7. Honest limits

  • Dispatch quality is bounded by the frontier's area: coverage (3% today, wave-13's §5 hygiene arm), not by this bridge.
  • The SessionStart-claim race (two dispatchers, or a human already on the task): today the loser's SessionStart claim just 409s and exits 0. The reserved claim-before-spawn dispatch (wave-13's atomic multi-claim) closes it.
  • No heartbeat endpoint exists — liveness is renew-or-expire; the 300s TTL + task.lease_expired → resume is the whole model.
  • The exact cmux new-surface flag spelling (--env vs -e, --prompt vs --initial-prompt, --type agent-session) is from feasibility research; dispatch is dry-run-first precisely so the operator eyeballs the invocation, and the slice confirms flags against cmux new-surface --help in one place.
§

Task tree: goal cmux-bridge-goal with children cb-worker-id, cb-hook-entrypoint, cb-hook-failsafe, cb-status-verb, cb-install-print, cb-dispatch-verb, cb-install-merge, cb-docs-card (+ reserved cb-next-frontier-claim). Linked into the dispatch-frontier family — it consumes taskboard.Frontier (df-frontier-fn).
